page_data.en:
Form 2
C. I. D.
I. O. REG
Shanghai Municipal Police. No. 192
Date 21/3/16.
Central Police Station.
March 20th 1916.
REPORT ON Newspaper Report re Censors in Chinese Post Office
Made by D.S.Givens Forwarded by
Sir,
Regarding attached, I beg to report that inquiries go to
show that the statement about police officers being employed as
censors in the Post Office is not correct. The censoring
of letters in the C.P.O. is done by a civil officer named Zee
( 徐 ), who has been specially appointed for the purpose.
As a matter of fact only very few of the letters passing through
the post office are censored.
I am, Sir,
Your Obedient Servant,
D.S.Givens
Detective Sergeant.
Chief Detective Inspector.
1/3

1916年3月20日。

由警佐吉文斯 (D.S.Givens) 呈报，转呈
阁下，
关于附件，谨报告称，经查询显示，有关警务人员受雇担任邮局检查员的说法并不属实。中华邮政总局 (C.P.O.) 的信件检查工作由一名名为徐 (Zee) 的文职官员负责，该员系为此目的特别任命。事实上，经由邮局流通的信件中，仅有极少数受到检查。

page_data.en:
Asiatic Daily
News
15-3-16

Policemen assist in examining letters at the Chinese
Post Office.
Formerly there was only a censor appointed at the
C.P.O. by the Government but since the Yunnan rebellion,
many letters with seditious contents have been
discovered and Governor Yang has despatched four more
deputies to the Post Office for duty in order
to properly carry out the censoring work. This
took effect last month. Since then the censors
have found the work much increased and they are
unable to go thoroughly into the documents as the
foreign employees in the Post offices often interfere
with them if they take a long time in carefully
examining a letter. In view of this Governor Yang
ordered Chief of Police Zee to send, commencing from
this month, two senior Police Officers to the Post
office to assist in the work. The censors are
divided into 2 parties, one to attend office in
the forenoon and the other in the afternoon.
With the exception of those addressed to public yamens
and proper business hongs, all letters intended for
private individuals are opened and read by the censors
and if found in order are re-sealed with a stamp
on bearing the characters "Examined by Censors
from the Woosung and Shanghai Governor's yamen.
Detection of letters.
Recently many discoveries have been made by the
censors. Some are letters written with chemical
liquid which are invisible until they are put into
water or held before a light or fire. Others are in
code quite unintelligible to an outsider. These
documents are always detained and brought to the
Governor's yamen nightly by the censors.
Enquiries will be made into them if necessary.

Letter from Dong Chih Yau 唐繼堯 found.
Shanghai being the centre of communications, letters
from Yunnan to other places must pass the local post office.
The day before yesterday the censors found two
letters which came from Yunnan and which signed by
Tong Chih Yau 唐繼堯 (the rebel Chiangchun of Yunnan)
were intended for ex-Viceroy Chen Chuan Huan. 考春宣
These documents were considered so important
that they were, immediately after being shown to
Governor Yang, forwarded to the Generalissimo's office
Peking for consideration.

Sin Wan Pao
In view of the rumour that the rebels in the
south are going to establish a Parliament of their
own, the politicians in Peking have requested the
President to speedily dissolve the present Chan Chingyuan
(Constitutional Bureau) and establish the Li Fah yuen
with members to be elected from the various provinces.
The Republicans in the south despite the measures
adopted by the Peking Government, are still endeavouring
to convene a citizens meeting in Shanghai for the
purpose of establishing a Parliament. 200 or 300
ex-members of the Parliament which was dissolved
in the 2nd year of the Republic, have arrived in
Shanghai. The first meeting they propose to hold in
Hardoon's garden.

Sing Kou Pao
Telegram from Peking.
The various Foreign Ministers in Peking received
an urgent wire from their Consuls in Chungking
on the 14th and immediately held a meeting in a very
secret manner. It is imagined that the Yunan soldiers
have reached the neighbourhood of Chungking and
commenced the attack on the Government troops
and that the various Consuls to ensure safety of the
foreigners at that port, requested instructions
how to proceed.
page_data.zh:
《亚细亚日报》
1916年3月15日

警察协助检查中国邮政局的信件。
此前，政府仅在中华邮政总局 (C.P.O.) 任命了一名检查员，但自云南叛乱以来，发现许多含有煽动性内容的信件，杨督军已增派四名副手前往邮局任职，以便妥善开展检查工作。此项措施于上月生效。此后，检查员发现工作量大幅增加，且无法对文件进行彻底审查，因为若他们花费较长时间仔细检查信件，邮局的外籍雇员往往会加以干涉。鉴于此，杨督军命令警察厅长徐 (Zee) 自本月起派遣两名高级警官前往邮局协助工作。检查员分为两组，一组在上午办公，另一组在下午办公。
除寄往各公署及正当商号的信件外，所有寄给私人的信件均由检查员拆阅，若未发现异常，则加盖印有“吴淞上海护军使署检查员验讫”字样的印章后重新封口。
信件的查获。
近期，检查员有许多发现。有些信件是用化学液体书写的，只有放入水中或置于灯光或火光前才能显现字迹。另一些则使用外人完全无法理解的密码。这些文件均被扣留，并由检查员每晚送至护军使署。如有必要，将对此进行调查。

查获唐继尧 (Tong Chih Yau) 的信件。
上海作为通讯中心，从云南发往其他地方的信件必须经过本地邮局。前天，检查员发现两封来自云南的信件，署名者为唐继尧（云南叛军将军），收件人为前总督陈宦 (Chen Chuan Huan)。考春宣（原文不清，疑似人名误植或OCR错误）
这些文件被认为极其重要，因此在呈交杨督军过目后，立即转送北京大元帅府审议。

《新闻报》
鉴于南方叛军拟自行设立议会的传闻，北京政界人士已请求总统迅速解散目前的参政院 (Chan Chingyuan)，并建立立法院 (Li Fah yuen)，其成员由各省选举产生。尽管北京政府采取了相应措施，南方的共和党人仍试图在上海召开公民会议，旨在设立议会。民国二年被解散的议会的前议员约二三百人已抵达上海。他们提议在哈同花园 (Hardoon's garden) 举行首次会议。

《申报》
北京电报。
驻北京的各国公使于14日收到其驻重庆领事的紧急电报，并立即以高度保密的方式举行了会议。据推测，云南军队已抵达重庆附近，并开始攻击政府军，各国领事为确保该港口外国人的安全，请求指示如何行事。

page_data.en:
Si Pao.
The Chiangchun of Nanking has received information
to the effect that Rebels Cheu Chah Sung 詹曉生 and
Dien Doong 田桐 have returned to Shanghai from Japan,
bringing with him a large sum of money with which they
have purchased several tens of rifles and concealed them
in the Tsiao San 椒山 mountain near the Tah Ho Lake,
Soochow, and that they are trying to induce the brigands
there to join them for the purpose of starting a rising.
He has consequently sent detectives to the place in
question to make a strict search and instructed the
authorities in Soochow and Shanghai to search the trains
and steamers for firearms.

The day before yesterday a man named Yih Sze 葉四
was arrested by the Police at Kau Ka Hong 高家行 ,
Pootung, for being in possession of a revolver, and was
transferred to the Police Court in the City at 1 p.m.
yesterday.

A Peking telegram reports that sometime ago the opium
merchants in Shanghai offered the Government $2,000,000
subscription to the war fund for an extension of the
term of the suppression of the opium trade by 9 months,
but this was rejected by the Ministry of Finance. Now
the Government, being in urgent need of money, has
proposed a compromise. Yesterday the Ministry of Finance
despatched a telegram to Mr. Tsai 蔡 , the Special
Commissioner of Opium Trade, informing him that the request
by the opium merchants regarding the suppression of the
opium trade should be dealt with by the Ministry of Home
Affairs and that he could communicate directly with that
Ministry on the subject. These words do not differentiate
in meaning from the declaration of the cancellation of
the rejection of the former request, and the question of
the monetary offer will soon be revived.

Min Sin Pao.
Four men named Wu Ching San 吳景山 , Yien Tuh Sung 顏德生
Tong Ah Nyi 湯阿二 and Li Yung Su 李永蘇 were shot
at the Military Commissioner's yamen yesterday. They
were handed over by the French Mixed Court on a charge
of concealing bombs in the Yung Hsing Lodginghouse 永興
and in a house in the Ong Nyeu Li alleyway 翁牛里 ,
Frenchtown.

Hua Pao.
On the afternoon of the day before yesterday the
robbers who participated in the robbery on the Ying
Ziang cash shop 盈祥 No. 3252 Seward Road and who
were arrested by the Hongkew Police, were brought up
on remand before the Mixed Court, Magistrate Wong Zau
Ts 王肇三 and British Assessor sat to hear the case.
Mr. Newman, the Police Legal Assistant, prosecuted. He
asked the Court to hand these robbers over to the
Chinese Authorities to be dealt with according to law.
The Court after hearing the statements of the prisoners,
gave judgement to hand them over to the City Court of
Procuration together with the pistols and ammunition
found in their possession.

Min E Pao.
A Hongkong telegram reports that Chiangchun Loh
Yung Ding 陸榮廷 of Kwangsi has declared his province
independent.

A telegram from Nanking says that the rebels have
raised over 2,000 men in the Kwang Tuh 廣德 and Ziao
Hu 巢湖 districts who have gone to the Tah Ho 太湖
Lake to start a rising. Plenty of firearms have been
seized.

《四报》（注：此处原文为 Si Pao，可能指某特定报刊，暂直译）
南京将军获悉，叛军周兆松 (Cheu Chah Sung) 和田桐 (Dien Doong) 已从日本返回上海，携带巨款，购买了数十支步枪，并将其藏匿于苏州太湖附近的椒山 (Tsiao San)。他们正试图诱使当地匪徒加入，以发动起义。因此，他已派遣侦探前往该地进行严密搜查，并指令苏州和上海当局在火车和轮船上搜查枪支。

前天，一名名为叶四 (Yih Sze) 的男子因持有左轮手枪，在浦东高家行 (Kau Ka Hong) 被警察逮捕，并于昨天下午1时被移送至城内警察法庭。

北京电报称，不久前，上海的鸦片商人向政府提供200万美元捐款作为战费，以换取将禁止鸦片贸易的期限延长9个月，但该请求被财政部拒绝。如今，由于政府急需资金，已提出妥协方案。昨天，财政部向鸦片贸易特派员蔡先生 (Mr. Tsai) 发出电报，告知他关于禁止鸦片贸易的请求应由内务部处理，他可直接就该事项与内务部联系。这番话在意义上无异于宣布撤销此前对该请求的拒绝，金钱捐赠的问题很快将重新提起。

《民新报》
四名名为吴景山 (Wu Ching San)、颜德生 (Yien Tuh Sung)、汤阿二 (Tong Ah Nyi) 和李永苏 (Li Yung Su) 的男子昨天在军事长官公署被枪决。他们是由法国会审公廨移交的，罪名是在法租界永兴旅馆 (Yung Hsing Lodginghouse) 及翁牛里 (Ong Nyeu Li) 的一处房屋内藏匿炸弹。

《华报》
前天下午，参与抢劫西华德路 (Seward Road) 3252号盈祥钱庄 (Ying Ziang cash shop) 并被虹口警察逮捕的劫匪，被提押至会审公廨受审，由推事王肇三 (Wong Zau Ts) 和英国陪审官坐堂审理。警方法律助理纽曼先生 (Mr. Newman) 提起公诉。他请求法庭将这些劫匪移交给中国当局依法处置。法庭在听取囚犯陈述后，判决将他们连同在其身上搜获的手枪和弹药一并移交给地方检察厅。

《民益报》
香港电报称，广西将军陆荣廷 (Loh Yung Ding) 已宣布其省份独立。

南京电报称，叛军在广德 (Kwang Tuh) 和巢湖 (Ziao Hu) 地区已招募超过2000人，这些人已前往太湖 (Tah Ho) 发动起义。大量枪支已被缴获。
